questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose LMU in Munich as my destination due to its high academic standards and the many historical sights in the city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was intended to be quite easy to get the information you need upon arrival, but at least half of the links sent out in the information emails weren’t working. The websites of LMU are quite hard to navigate, so it takes a while to find the relevant information if the links don’t work properly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: LMU sent out information emails and had information meetings.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is quite hard to find a place to live in Munich, and the rent is at least as high as in Copenhagen. I highly recommend looking for housing as soon as possible so you don’t end up with a high rent and a small room. There are lots of free websites that list vacant rooms and flats, and LMU will also provide these websites.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is quite expensive

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
At the Department of Economics, course registration is different from all other departments at LMU.
You can shuffle around courses and choose the ones you find interesting without registering for them in advance. Course registration only takes place when you register for exams in the middle or at the end of the lecture period.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was an introduction meeting that explained the process, but the international office could also be contacted for further information.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I only got one of the classes I wanted when I applied for the exchange at LMU since the classes weren’t offered when the final course catalog was provided just before the semester started.
However, registering for classes was quite easy.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Don't fix your mind on specific courses before the final catalog is provided, as it can change quite a bit.
Be aware that exchange students can't take any courses from the quantitative economics track, as these are only available to full-time students at LMU.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was similar to the level at UCPH, but the exams are taken with pen and paper, which makes them a bit harder.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I didn’t really like the teaching style in most of the courses at LMU.
The professor conducted both the lectures and the tutorials, and often, the material could just as easily be studied at home with the same outcome.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
The courses I was enrolled in were:

- Development Economics
- Monetary Economics
- Topics in Climate and Resource Economics
- Nonparametric Econometrics
- Labor Economics

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Labor Economics because it consists of only one month of lectures and had good teaching. I would also recommend Nonparametric Econometrics, as the exam is based on six hand-in assignments and is very useful.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn’t encounter any unexpected costs, but it’s good to have some savings if you want to attend student trips.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Overall, I would say that Munich is fairly cheaper than Copenhagen in terms of food, drinks, and leisure activities. However, rent can be quite high depending on what you find.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: ESN (Erasmus Student Network) organized many activities such as parties, day trips, weekend trips, pub crawls, karaoke nights, and lots of other events. They have an event calendar for the entire semester, and I would highly recommend attending as many as possible because it is an amazing place to meet people in the same situation as yourself.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There are some sports clubs, but I didn’t attend any of them.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Use the Deutschland Ticket to travel around Bavaria and join the trips hosted by ESN.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I didn’t find it too challenging.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be shy! Many local students come from other countries or different parts of Germany and are very friendly if you just give it a chance and put yourself out there.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find it challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Beer gardens and bars are very welcoming, and if tables are full, people don’t mind making room for strangers if you just ask them."

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open-minded and step out of your comfort zone.
Enjoy the nature and outdoor life of the city whenever you can.
Interact with the German students—they often know the answers to many of the questions you may have about studying at LMU and life in Munich.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: They are not very technical at LMU, so don’t get stressed out if the platforms and online information aren’t the best.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of the exchange was probably being on my own and having to build a new social network with students from different cultures and countries.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Studying for the exams was challenging. In Germany, old exam sets are not provided, so the structure of the exam is somewhat unknown, which made preparing for the exams even harder.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
